prompt: What is the main reason to enable rack-zone awareness on a Redis Software cluster?
explanation: Rack-zone awareness exists so the cluster survives losing an entire rack or zone: primaries and their replicas (plus endpoints) are spread across racks, so when one rack fails the replicas and endpoints in the remaining racks take over. It does not speed up replication, it has nothing to do with key redirection or backups, and it is about placement guarantees, not the minimum node count.

options.text: So the cluster stays available when an entire rack or zone fails
To make shard-to-shard replication faster within a rack
To reduce MOVED redirects for cluster-aware clients
To allow backups to be stored on a different rack
